transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hello, Doctor. Well, what finally got me to come in is that my concentration has just gotten really unreliable lately. I'll be at the clinic reviewing a patient's chart, or even just at home laying out a watercolor wash, and... suddenly I realize I've read the same line three times. My mind just keeps wandering off to everything that could possibly go wrong.
When did you first begin having this concentration difficulty?
Well, let me think... I'd say this has really been going on since I started the formal retirement process at the practice. That was about a year and three months ago.
Are your worries mainly about retiring, or do they also involve many other parts of your life?

It's really a mix of things. My mind just keeps circling around all sorts of different issues. I'll worry about whether my old patients are being looked after properly by the new staff, or if the financial side of the practice handoff is completely sound. And then I worry about myself, too—whether I’ll just become useless once I’m fully retired. It feels like it touches everything, and honestly, the amount of worrying I do feels out of proportion even to me.
On how many days in a typical week do you find yourself worrying like this?

I'm not exactly sure, to be honest. I haven't really kept track of a specific number of days. It just feels like it's happening a lot of the time, but... yeah, I couldn't give you an exact count for a typical week.
When the worrying starts, do you find it difficult to control or stop it?

Yes, I really do. It's very hard to stop once it gets going. I try to reason with myself, sort of the way I would talk to a nervous patient in my chair, but... it just doesn't work. One concern just leads right into the next one. Eventually, instead of letting it go, I end up checking my emails, reviewing practice notes, or asking the staff the same questions all over again. I just can't seem to turn it off.
During the past six months, on how many days per week has this worrying occurred?

I mean, like I said, I haven't really kept a strict count. If I had to guess over the last six months... I don't know, it just feels like it's most days. I really couldn't give you a specific number per week.
How much are these worries and concentration problems interfering with your work, home life, or daily activities?

It's definitely getting in the way. At work, I’ve actually had to slow down and... well, postpone parts of the retirement handoff for the practice. I just keep second-guessing my decisions and end up losing time at the clinic. And at home, even my hobbies, like my painting and gardening, they just don’t feel as manageable as they used to.
Before the retirement process began, were you already having this kind of difficulty concentrating?

No, not really. It wasn't an issue before all this. The trouble focusing and all the worrying... it really just started when I began the formal retirement process. That was about a year and three months ago.
During the past six months, has this excessive worrying occurred on more days than not?
Yes, I would say so. Like I mentioned a minute ago, it really feels like it happens most days. So, yes, definitely on more days than not.
Have you been feeling unusually restless or on edge during this period of worrying?
No, not really. I haven't noticed feeling restless or... on edge, physically. It's mostly just the constant thoughts in my head, rather than feeling keyed up or anything like that.
Have you been experiencing muscle tension during this period of excessive worrying?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. My muscles feel fine, really. Like I was saying, it's mostly just the mental part—the constant worrying—rather than feeling physically tight or sore anywhere.
Have you been having trouble sleeping during this period of excessive worrying?

Yes, I have. I usually get into bed feeling pretty tired, but... well, as soon as the house gets quiet, my mind just starts going. I start replaying patient transfers from the office, or going over money details in my head. And even when I do manage to fall asleep, I'm usually up by four or five in the morning, just feeling like I never really settled down or got a proper rest.
If the retirement process and practice handoff were fully resolved, do you think you would still be worrying this way about other areas of your life?

I'm really not sure. It's... hard to say, because right now the practice and the retirement are just taking up so much space in my head. I haven't really thought about what it would be like if it were all completely settled. So, I don't know if my mind would just find something else to stress over or if things would finally quiet down. I just don't know.
When you are not feeling worried, do you still have trouble concentrating?

No, I don't think so. If I actually have a moment where I'm not worrying about the practice or things like that, my focus is fine. I can read or get through whatever I need to do without any issues. It's really only when my mind is racing that I get distracted.
Is the retirement and practice handoff still actively ongoing, or has it already been completed?
It's still ongoing. We're right in the middle of it, actually. There's just a lot of moving parts right now with the paperwork and the transition, so it's definitely not finished yet.
